name: @guardbee/security-suite

tools.name: owasp_scan_path
tools.description: Run a unified OWASP MCP Top 10 scan over a filesystem path — orchestrates secret, server, oauth, audit-gap, context-oversharing, toxic-flow, and tool-poisoning auditors; returns A–F grade.

discoverShadow.description: Also discover Shadow MCP on this host (MCP09)

allowlistPath.description: Allowlist file for Shadow MCP discover

tools.name: owasp_scan_live
tools.description: Connect to a live MCP server (stdio or HTTP), call tools/list, then grade toxic-flow + tool-poisoning (MCP03/MCP10).

tools.name: owasp_scan_catalog
tools.description: Audit a tools/list JSON dump for toxic flows and tool-description poisoning (MCP03/MCP10).

catalog.description: JSON string: { tools: [...] } or a bare tools array

tools.name: list_owasp_coverage
tools.description: List OWASP MCP Top 10 categories and which GuardBee scanners cover them in this meta-scan

tools.name: secrets_scan_text
tools.description: Scan a text string or code snippet for exposed secrets and API keys

label.description: Optional label shown in findings (e.g. filename)

entropy.description: Also flag random-looking values assigned to secret-like names (default true)

tools.name: secrets_scan_file
tools.description: Scan a single file for exposed secrets and API keys

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the file to scan

entropy.description: Also flag random-looking values assigned to secret-like names (default true)

tools.name: secrets_scan_directory
tools.description: Recursively scan a directory for exposed secrets and API keys. Automatically skips node_modules, .git, dist, and binary files.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the directory to scan

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to scan (default: 5000)

include.description: Only scan files whose path contains one of these strings (e.g. [".env", ".ts"])

exclude.description: Skip files/dirs whose path contains one of these strings

baseline.description: Path to a baseline file: only findings not in it are reported

entropy.description: Also flag random-looking values assigned to secret-like names (default true)

tools.name: secrets_scan_git
tools.description: Scan a git repository for secrets in what git says was added: the staged changes (before a commit) or every commit's added lines (history). History finds secrets that were deleted from the files but are still in the repository.

path.description: A directory inside the git repository

mode.description: staged: lines added in the index; history: lines added by each commit

range.description: History only: a revision range such as main..HEAD (default: all refs)

maxCommits.description: History only: stop after this many commits

baseline.description: Path to a baseline file: only findings not in it are reported

entropy.description: Also flag random-looking values assigned to secret-like names (default true)

tools.name: secrets_scan_agent_history
tools.description: Scan the transcripts coding agents keep on this machine (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Continue) for secrets that were pasted into a chat or printed by a command. Such a secret was already sent to the model provider and should be rotated. Each secret is reported once with how often it appears.

entropy.description: Also flag random-looking values assigned to secret-like names (default false here: transcripts hold a lot of code)

tools.name: secrets_list_patterns
tools.description: List all secret patterns that the scanner can detect

tools.name: injection_scan_text
tools.description: Scan a text string — a RAG chunk, a scraped web page, a document, a tool result — for indirect prompt injection payloads (instruction-override phrases, spoofed chat-template roles, hidden/invisible text, content addressing 'the AI' directly, data-exfiltration attempts) before it reaches a model's context.

label.description: Optional label shown in findings (e.g. source URL or filename)

tools.name: injection_scan_file
tools.description: Scan a single file (a knowledge-base document, an HTML page, extracted text) for indirect prompt injection payloads

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the file to scan

tools.name: injection_scan_directory
tools.description: Recursively scan a directory — e.g. a RAG knowledge base or a corpus of scraped pages — for indirect prompt injection payloads. Automatically skips node_modules, .git, dist, and binary files.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the directory to scan

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to scan (default: 5000)

include.description: Only scan files whose path contains one of these strings (e.g. [".md", "knowledge-base/"])

exclude.description: Skip files/dirs whose path contains one of these strings

tools.name: injection_list_patterns
tools.description: List all indirect prompt injection patterns that the scanner can detect, grouped by category

tools.name: toxic_flow_audit_catalog
tools.description: Audit a tools/list-shaped JSON catalog for the lethal trifecta (toxic flow): untrusted content + sensitive/private data + exfiltration or destruction on the same MCP server. Returns an A–F grade.

catalog.description: JSON array of tools, or { tools: [...] } from tools/list

tools.name: toxic_flow_scan_source
tools.description: Scan TypeScript/JavaScript MCP server source for .registerTool(...) and .tool(...) registrations and audit them for toxic flows

tools.name: toxic_flow_scan_file
tools.description: Scan a single source file for toxic flows

tools.name: toxic_flow_scan_directory
tools.description: Recursively scan a directory of MCP server source for toxic flows across all registered tools

tools.name: toxic_flow_explain_trifecta
tools.description: Explain the lethal trifecta / toxic-flow model this auditor uses

tools.name: mcp_config_scan_config_text
tools.description: Scan an MCP client config JSON string (Cursor mcp.json, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, or VS Code) for unpinned packages, secrets, wildcard auto-approve, unauthenticated remote endpoints, and typosquats.

tools.name: mcp_config_scan_file
tools.description: Scan one MCP client config file, or a SKILL.md agent skill when the file has that name.

tools.name: mcp_config_scan_skill_text
tools.description: Scan one agent SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter plus body) for unrestricted allowed-tools, instruction override, credential file reads, and literal secrets. Name collisions across skills require a directory scan.

tools.name: mcp_config_scan_directory
tools.description: Find mcp.json, mcp_config.json, claude_desktop_config.json, and SKILL.md under a directory and audit each one. A directory scan also compares skill names. Does not start any MCP server.

exclude.description: Skip paths containing one of these strings

tools.name: mcp_config_scan_inventory
tools.description: Detect cross-server tool shadowing from an inventory of tool catalogs. Pass the tool names and descriptions already collected from each installed server. This tool does not connect to those servers.

tools.name: mcp_config_discover_shadow_mcp
tools.description: OWASP MCP09:2025 — discover MCP client configs in well-known host paths (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, VS Code, Claude Code) and flag servers that are not on an organization allowlist (Shadow MCP). Does not start any MCP server.

allowlist.description: JSON allowlist: {"names":["filesystem"],"packages":["@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem"],"hosts":["mcp.example.com"]} or line form name:/package:/host:

home.description: Override home directory used to resolve well-known config paths

includeContentAudit.description: Also run the normal config content checks on each discovered file (default false)

tools.name: mcp_config_list_host_config_paths
tools.description: List the well-known MCP client config paths this auditor checks during shadow (MCP09) discovery on the current OS.

tools.name: mcp_config_list_patterns
tools.description: List the MCP config, agent skill, shadow-MCP discovery, and cross-server shadowing checks, with their OWASP MCP Top 10 tags.

tools.name: deps_audit_npm
tools.description: Audit npm dependencies for known CVEs using the OSV database. Reads exact versions from package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock (v1 and berry) or bun.lock, falling back to package.json ranges

directory.description: Path to the directory containing package.json

includeDevDeps.description: Include devDependencies in the audit (default: false)

exploitData.description: Add CISA KEV (exploited in the wild) and FIRST EPSS data and order findings by it (default: true; sends CVE IDs only)

tools.name: deps_audit_pip
tools.description: Audit Python dependencies for known CVEs using the OSV database. Reads exact versions from uv.lock, poetry.lock or Pipfile.lock, falling back to requirements.txt / pyproject.toml

directory.description: Path to the directory containing requirements.txt or pyproject.toml

includeDevDeps.description: Include dev groups from poetry.lock, uv.lock or Pipfile.lock (default: false)

exploitData.description: Add CISA KEV (exploited in the wild) and FIRST EPSS data and order findings by it (default: true; sends CVE IDs only)

tools.name: deps_audit_package
tools.description: Audit a single package by name, version, and ecosystem

exploitData.description: Add CISA KEV (exploited in the wild) and FIRST EPSS data and order findings by it (default: true; sends CVE IDs only)

tools.name: deps_audit_directory
tools.description: Auto-detect and audit every supported project in a directory: npm (package-lock, pnpm, yarn, bun), Python (uv, Poetry, Pipenv, requirements), Rust (Cargo.lock), Go (go.mod), Ruby (Gemfile.lock) and PHP (composer.lock)

directory.description: Path to the project root directory

exploitData.description: Add CISA KEV (exploited in the wild) and FIRST EPSS data and order findings by it (default: true; sends CVE IDs only)
